skill.name: convex-performance-audit
skill.description: Audits Convex application performance using signals from insights, code paths, and reference playbooks for reads, writes, subscriptions, and function limits.
skill.summary: Diagnose slow or expensive Convex features and choose safe performance fixes.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting and Convex ctx.db examples in documentation. Two findings are confirmed because the skill instructs agents to run npx-based Convex CLI commands, including a latest-package fallback that should require explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to run npx commands for Convex insights.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Convex CLI diagnostics, and prefer the project-installed CLI when available.

remediation.issue: The fallback command uses npx -y convex@latest.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid automatic latest-package execution; ask the user before downloading packages or recommend a pinned version.

content.value_statement: Convex performance issues can come from broad reads, write contention, reactive invalidation, or function limits. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through targeted diagnosis and safe fixes.
actual_capabilities: Routes performance symptoms to focused guidance for hot reads, OCC conflicts, subscriptions, or function budgets.
Uses Convex insights, dashboard signals, or code review to identify the most relevant bottleneck.
Provides fix order guidance for indexes, digest tables, batching, no-op writes, and point-in-time reads.
Encourages sibling reader and writer audits so one optimized path is not left inconsistent with related code.
Includes verification checklists for result correctness, reduced work, and migration-safe rollouts.
limitations: Requires a Convex application or Convex codebase to be useful.
Runtime metrics may be unavailable if the user cannot access deployment insights or logs.
Large schema or fetch strategy changes still need human product and rollout decisions.
The skill provides guidance; it does not automatically prove production performance improvements.

use_cases.title: Investigate a slow Convex page
use_cases.description: Trace the page calls, identify broad reads or large payloads, and choose the safest optimization path.

use_cases.title: Reduce write contention
use_cases.description: Analyze OCC conflicts, hot documents, and no-op writes before changing mutation design.

use_cases.title: Control subscription cost
use_cases.description: Review reactive query usage and decide where batching, skipping, or point-in-time reads are appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic performance audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a known slow feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Convex performance audit skill to review the slow dashboard page. Identify the likely problem class before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Use available insights output
prompt_templates.scenario: The user has Convex insights data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Convex insights output to prioritize performance fixes. Explain which functions or tables should be inspected first.

prompt_templates.title: Audit write contention
prompt_templates.scenario: The app has mutation retries or OCC conflicts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OCC conflict guidance to inspect these mutations. Look for broad read sets, hot documents, and unnecessary writes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration-safe optimization
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced change that may require schema or data rollout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Convex performance audit skill to propose a migration-safe optimization for this hot list query. Include sibling readers, write paths, fallback behavior, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: A project list page is slow and reads many documents.
output: The audit identifies read amplification as the primary problem class.
It recommends checking indexes and return shapes before adding digest tables.
It lists sibling list queries that should be inspected for the same pattern.

output_examples.input: Deployment health shows frequent OCC conflicts on votes.
output: The audit focuses on hot document contention and broad read sets.
It suggests no-op write checks and possible counter sharding only if metrics justify it.
It includes verification using conflict rate and mutation latency.

output_examples.input: A React page has too many live Convex subscriptions.
output: The audit separates product freshness needs from backend subscription cost.
It recommends batching related data and using skip for missing arguments.
It flags low-freshness flows as candidates for point-in-time reads.

best_practices: Start from measured signals when available, then inspect the matching code paths.
Fix sibling readers and writers together when they touch the same table family.
Verify behavior, fallback paths, and performance signals before closing the audit.
anti_patterns: Do not add digest tables or denormalized fields without evidence of a hot path.
Do not replace all reactivity with point-in-time reads when users need live updates.
Do not optimize one function while leaving sibling functions on the same costly pattern.

faq.question: Does this skill require Convex insights output?
faq.answer: No. Insights output is preferred, but the skill can audit code when runtime signals are unavailable.

faq.question: Can it help with OCC conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for hot documents, broad read sets, no-op writes, and scheduled secondary work.

faq.question: Does it always recommend denormalization?
faq.answer: No. It treats denormalization and digest tables as tradeoffs for measured or clearly unbounded hot paths.

faq.question: Can it review React subscription behavior?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers useQuery, usePaginatedQuery, skip behavior, batching, and point-in-time read choices.

faq.question: Will it make production changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through analysis and safe implementation decisions.

faq.question: Is it only for backend engineers?
faq.answer: No. It is useful for full-stack, frontend, and backend engineers working on Convex performance.
